notes: One source for Agentlas web search on the desktop (bundled Agentlas browser, no window) and the phone (the app's own WebView, off screen). Copied byte for byte with web-search-serp.js into the phone app; tests on each side hold the copies equal. No search API and no key: a real browser engine opens the search site's own result page and web-search-serp.js reads it. The engine is never disguised beyond `userAgent` below, never clicks, types or solves a check: a blocked or off-topic page moves to the next engine, and when every engine is blocked the tool answers `search_blocked` so the person can search in the browser themself. Measured: DuckDuckGo and Bing answer the Agentlas browser; Google answers an automated browser with its check page.
userAgent: The engine's own user agent, with the token `HeadlessChrome` written `Chrome` where the engine runs without a window, and ` Agentlas/<app version>` appended. Nothing else is changed: the reader says it is the Agentlas app's browser, as a WebView or an Electron window does.

fields.url: https absolute address the tool itself opened or the search page listed (never an address a model wrote)
fields.title: the page or result title as the page gave it, 1-300 characters; the host when there is none
fields.snippet: optional, the search result's own description, at most 500 characters
fields.kind: `search` (a result listed by a search page) or `page` (a page the tool opened and read)

source.order: pages that were opened and read first, in the order they were read; then search results in the order the searches listed them; one entry per address
